 Pallet Networks Aug 28, 2026 

# Hawks Haulage joins Palletways UK network

Leicester-based logistics provider, Hawks Haulage, has joined the Palletways UK network, marking a key milestone in its strategic growth plans.

Founded in 2019 by Pardeep Virk as a single-truck operation, the company has rapidly grown into a thriving, family-run logistics outfit, now operating a fleet of 35 vehicles and employing 40 staff.

The decision to join Palletways – Europe’s largest express palletised freight network – represents a strategic move to further enhance the business’ offering to customers, while maintaining the personalised service that has underpinned Hawks Haulage’s success.

It comes amid major growth plans which also include further fleet expansions, technological upgrades, staff development and investment in a new state-of-the-art warehouse facility capable of storing up to 2,500 pallets.

This development is set to strengthen the firm’s operational infrastructure, enabling greater efficiency, improving storage solutions and supporting future expansion into integrated logistics services.

# Family food business opens landmark DC

Posted on Monday 3 August 2026 Share: 

Family-owned fine foods manufacturer and distributor, Bramble Foods has opened a new 67,000 ft2 distribution centre in Market Harborough, Leicestershire, East Midlands.

By Liza Helps, Property Editor, Logistics Matters

THE COMPANY pre-let the facility on the final phase of Leicestershire Council’s Airfield Business Park last year. It currently leases a unit on and will be taking the additional new unit to further expand their growing business.

The state-of-the-art facility becomes Bramble Foods’ main national distribution hub, significantly increasing warehousing and distribution capacity while supporting the company’s expanding portfolio of premium food brands which includes Whitakers Chocolates, The Bay Tree and Lings.

Airfield Business Park was first opened in 2019 and is home to 14 businesses.

The new facility known as Lancaster House includes a number of sustainability features and boasts an EPC A+ rating of A+, a 50kW solar array that should save between 45,000 and 50,000 kWh a year as well as two electric vehicle charging points.

# Camco Chemical Announces 130,000-Square-Foot Northern Kentucky Distribution Expansion

 Published on Wednesday, September 2, 2026 by Nicole Shakir, Managing Editor of Expansion Solutions Magazine 

### New Independence facility will expand fulfillment, warehousing and supply chain capacity for the family-owned manufacturer

INDEPENDENCE, Ky. (September 2, 2026) — RSA Properties LLC and Camco Chemical have announced plans to construct a new 130,000-square-foot warehouse and distribution center on Camco Chemical’s existing Holton Drive campus in Independence, Kentucky.

The new facility will expand Camco’s fulfillment and distribution capacity while strengthening its broader supply chain capabilities and supporting continued growth across its contract manufacturing operations in Northern Kentucky.

RSA Properties, the family-owned real estate entity developing the project, will work with Furlong Building as contractor. Once complete, Camco Chemical will integrate the facility into its existing operations.

# L’entreprise familiale FM Logistic, a ouvert une nouvelle plateforme de… 30 000 m2 à Saint-Georges-d’Espéranche

Posté par dominique | 28 Juil, 2026 | A la une de Vienne, Economie Vienne | 0 | 

FM Logistic s’implante encore un peu plus dans le bassin lyonnais. Elle a investi depuis septembre 2025 une plateforme logistique à Saint-Georges-d’Espéranche,. Le bâtiment longe la route de Lafayette en direction de Vienne.

Avec une superficie de 30 000 mètres carrés, l’entrepôt servira essentiellement à l’entreprise Gamm Vert, Sud et Est ; et ce, au service de son réseau de magasins.

FM Logistic s’est installé en tant que sous-traitant afin de regrouper, stocker et traiter les marchandises.

L’entrepôt logistique affiche une capacité annuelle de réception de 90 000 palettes.

Répartis en cinq cellules, le site a été pensé « pour absorber une forte saisonnalité tout en gérant une très grande diversité de produits », explique-t-on chez FM Logistic.
